commonsFile: File:Cuernos del Paine, Parque Nacional Torres del Paine, Chile1.jpg
attribution: Diego Delso — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Cuernos del Paine, Torres del Paine National Park, Magallanes Region
alt: The banded granite and dark sedimentary horns of the Cuernos del Paine rising above a turquoise lake
caption: The Cuernos del Paine, two-tone granite horns above Lago Nordenskjöld. Day 4 follows the shore trail beneath them to Los Cuernos camp, the scenic middle of the five-day W trek.

commonsFile: File:Cordillera Paine; vista desde el mirador Base de las Torres, Parque nacional Torres del Paine, Chile.jpg
attribution: CARLOS TEIXIDOR CADENAS — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Mirador Base de las Torres, Torres del Paine National Park
alt: The Paine granite towers above the moraine lake at the Base de las Torres viewpoint
caption: The three granite towers above their moraine lake from the Base de las Torres viewpoint. Day 4 starts in the dark so the group is here for sunrise, after a night at Chileno, before the long walk west.

commonsFile: File:Cerro Paine Grande, glaciar, río y valle del Francés, Cordillera Paine, Magallanes, Chile.jpg
attribution: CARLOS TEIXIDOR CADENAS — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Valle del Francés, Cordillera Paine, Magallanes Region
alt: Cerro Paine Grande with its hanging glacier above the Francés river valley
caption: Cerro Paine Grande and its hanging glacier at the head of the Francés Valley. Day 5 climbs into the valley's middle section from Los Cuernos, then continues to Paine Grande, the longest walking day of the W.

commonsFile: File:Glaciar Grey, Parque Nacional Torres del Paine, Chile4.jpg
attribution: Diego Delso — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Grey Glacier, Torres del Paine National Park
alt: The blue, crevassed front of Grey Glacier calving into Lago Grey with floating icebergs
caption: The front of Grey Glacier at the edge of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, with icebergs in Lago Grey. Day 6 is the walk from Paine Grande to the viewpoints and the Grey camp, the western end of the W.

attribution: Alexis Alvarez — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Paine Grande, Lago Pehoé shore, Torres del Paine National Park
alt: Paine Grande refugio and campsite at the shore of Lago Pehoé beneath the mountains
caption: The Paine Grande refugio and camping area on Lago Pehoé. The group pitches here on night 3 of the trek, and the catamaran dock for the exit on Day 7 is a short walk away.

commonsFile: File:Guanacos, Parque Nacional Torres del Paine, Chile5.jpg
attribution: Diego Delso — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Torres del Paine National Park, Magallanes Region
alt: A herd of guanacos on open steppe grassland with the Paine massif behind
caption: Guanacos on the steppe near Laguna Amarga. They are the park's most visible large mammal; the bus ride on Day 3 from Puerto Natales to the trailhead usually passes several herds.

attribution: Diego Delso — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Puerto Natales, Última Esperanza Province, Magallanes Region
alt: Puerto Natales waterfront on Última Esperanza Sound with mountains across the water
caption: The waterfront of Puerto Natales on Última Esperanza Sound. This small port town is the base for gear rental, supplies and the park bus, on nights 2 and 7.

commonsFile: File:Spheniscus magellanicus, Seno Otway, Tierra de Fuego, Chile1.jpg
attribution: Diego Delso — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Seno Otway penguin colony, near Punta Arenas
alt: A Magellanic penguin standing beside its burrow in coastal scrub at Seno Otway
caption: A Magellanic penguin at its burrow at Seno Otway, about an hour from Punta Arenas. Day 8 visits the colony in the afternoon; the breeding season ends around March, so adults and moulting young are still ashore on the group's dates.

commonsFile: File:Laguna del Castillo Parque Nacional Cerro Castillo 11.jpg
attribution: Natalia Reyes Escobar — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Laguna Cerro Castillo, Cerro Castillo National Park, Aysén Region
alt: A turquoise glacial lagoon beneath the jagged spires of Cerro Castillo
caption: The glacial lagoon beneath the spires of Cerro Castillo. Day 10 is the 14 km out-and-back hike from the village, the group's one proper mountain day on the Carretera Austral.

commonsFile: File:Lago General Carrera - Capillas de Mármol 4.jpg
attribution: Jpmorenosanchez — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Marble Caves, Lago General Carrera, Puerto Río Tranquilo
alt: Smooth blue-streaked marble caves and arches at the edge of Lago General Carrera
caption: The Marble Caves in Lago General Carrera, reached by small boat from Puerto Río Tranquilo. Day 11 goes in the morning, when the lake is usually calmer, and the swirling blue marble is brightest.

attribution: Lin linao — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Ventisquero Colgante, Queulat National Park, Aysén Region
alt: The Queulat hanging glacier spilling down a rock face above a lake
caption: The Queulat hanging glacier on its cliff above the lake. Day 13 walks the trail to the lake viewpoint, then ends the day at the hot springs near Puyuhuapi.

attribution: Rakela — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The unpaved Carretera Austral winding through forested hills and mountains
caption: A stretch of gravel on the Carretera Austral. South of Villa Cerro Castillo the road is mostly unpaved, so the group drives at about 60 km/h, with two licensed drivers sharing the days.
